settings.title: Settings
settings.markReadHint: Controls when an opened message counts as read.
settings.showPreviewText: Show preview text in the message list
settings.subjectOnlyHint: Hides sender, date and size and tightens the rows. The chosen columns are kept.
settings.readerPositionHint: Without a reading pane, messages open in the full area instead.
settings.unifiedFoldersHint: Combines inbox, sent, archive and so on across all accounts into one view each.
settings.blockRemoteImagesHint: Stops senders from tracking when you open a message via tracking pixels.
settings.attachmentCacheHint: Attachments of opened messages are stored locally and removed automatically after 30 days.
settings.confirmRemoveAccount: Remove this account? Locally cached messages will be deleted.
settings.matchModeAny: At least one condition must match
settings.vcardHint: vCard files (.vcf) are read and written by every address book, from Thunderbird through Outlook to a phone.
settings.ruleSkipped: "{{name}}" left out: {{reason}} cannot be expressed here.
settings.pgpRingHint: Only the active key signs and is handed out. The others stay because mail encrypted to them stays encrypted to them. Deleting one loses access to that mail.
settings.pgpNoKey: No PGP key set up for this account yet.
settings.pastePgpKey: Paste this contact's PGP public key
settings.notifications: Show desktop notifications for new mail
settings.newPasswordOptional: New password (leave blank to keep current)
settings.pgpConfirmDeleteKey: Delete this account's PGP key pair? Encrypted mail will no longer be readable.
settings.pgpPasteKeyPair: Paste your armored PGP private key (the public key is derived from it)
settings.pgpPublished: Published. Check your inbox for the verification mail from keys.openpgp.org.
settings.pgpKeyNotFound: No public key found for this address.
settings.syncIntervalHint: The inbox is watched continuously anyway. This setting covers all other folders.
settings.pgpSignHint: A signature proves the message is from you and was not altered in transit. It encrypts nothing, the content stays readable to everyone.
settings.fontScaleHint: Scales the whole interface, not just the message text.
settings.columnWidthHint: Widths can be dragged directly in the list, at the right edge of the column heading.
settings.warnSuspiciousLinks: Warn about suspicious links and senders
settings.warnSuspiciousLinksHint: Detects addresses that read differently than they resolve: letters rebuilt from other alphabets, invisible characters, a destination hidden behind an @, and link text naming a different domain than the target.
settings.confirmAllLinks: Ask before opening any external link
settings.confirmAllLinksHint: Including unremarkable ones. More thorough, but a prompt that always appears eventually gets clicked away unread.
settings.warnRiskyAttachmentsHint: Marks attachments that run a program when opened, and double extensions such as "invoice.pdf.exe".
settings.customThemeHint: Overrides individual colours of the chosen theme. Colours you do not set stay as the theme defines them.
settings.themeCopied: Colour scheme copied to the clipboard
settings.themeImportInvalid: That does not contain a valid colour scheme. Colours are expected as #rrggbb.
settings.themeContrast: {{token}} on {{against}} is hard to read at a contrast of {{ratio}}:1
settings.shortcutsHint: Click a shortcut and press the key you want.
settings.shortcutRejected: "{{key}}" cannot be assigned, because that key is needed to operate the app.
settings.shortcutConflict: Two actions share a shortcut. Only one of them will fire.
settings.identitiesHint: Several addresses under the same mailbox. All send over the same server; only the From line changes.
settings.identityLastKept: The last sender address of an account is kept, because without it nothing could be sent.
settings.tagsHint: Tags are stored as IMAP keywords on the server, so they are visible in webmail and on your phone too.
settings.tagKeywordHint: This is what the tag is called on the server. It stays the same even if you rename the tag.
settings.confirmDeleteTag: Delete tag "{{name}}"? Messages already tagged keep the keyword on the server.
settings.undoSendHint: The message only leaves after this time. Until then it can be called back, it never reached the server at all.
settings.pgpExpiringSoon_one: This key expires tomorrow. After that nobody will accept your signatures. Generate a new one and hand it out now.
settings.pgpExpiringSoon_other: This key expires in {{count}} days. After that nobody will accept your signatures. Generate a new one and hand it out in good time.

pgpHealth.expired: This key has expired. It still decrypts old mail, but new signatures are no longer accepted.
pgpHealth.revoked: This key has been revoked. It must not be used for anything new.

settings.pgpContactRingHint: Older keys are kept: a signature can only be checked against the key that made it.

riskDetail.ipAddressHost: The address is {{detail}} and so gives no name that would identify who runs it.
riskDetail.lookalikeDomain: Very close to "{{detail}}", which you deal with regularly, but not the same domain.

senderRisk.nameContainsOtherAddress: Display name states a different address
senderRisk.replyToMismatch: Replies would go to another domain
senderRisk.punycode: Sender domain is written in encoded form

links.bannerAuth: The server could not confirm this message's sender
links.bannerPixels_one: This message contains a tracking pixel
links.pixelDetail_one: An invisible image reports the message being opened. It only loads if you allow remote images.
links.pixelDetail_other: {{count}} invisible images report the message being opened. They only load if you allow remote images.

authFailed.spf: The sending server is not listed for this sender domain.
authFailed.dkim: The sender domain's signature is missing or does not match the content.

links.firstContactDetail: Nothing has ever arrived from this address before. That is unremarkable in itself, most first contacts are harmless. It is only worth a second look when money or credentials are being asked for.

refused.executable: The contents of this file are an executable program, whatever it is called. Peregrine does not launch those. Save it first if you genuinely trust it.
refused.mismatch: The contents of this file do not match its extension. That is exactly how a program is disguised as a document.

import.title: Import accounts from Thunderbird
import.noAccounts: The Thunderbird profile has no importable accounts.
import.passwordNote: Servers, ports and encryption are taken over. Passwords are not, because Thunderbird encrypts them against its own profile. Please enter one per account.
import.scanFailed: Could not read the Thunderbird profile

blocker.oauth2: Sign-in via Google/Microsoft is not supported yet

keyImport.sectionHint: Read keys from Thunderbird or from a file. Each key is matched to an account by the addresses in its user ID; other people's public keys are filed under the matching contact.
keyImport.title: Take over keys
keyImport.scanFailed: The keys could not be read
keyImport.noThunderbird: No Thunderbird profile with keys was found.
keyImport.emptyFile: This file contains no OpenPGP keys.
keyImport.thunderbirdSealed: Your own secret keys are in Thunderbird, but sealed with a passphrase Thunderbird generates itself and keeps in its own password store. Peregrine deliberately does not read that store. Other people's public keys can be taken over directly. For your own, use the export route (see the instructions).
keyImport.passphraseHint: The passphrase you set when exporting from Thunderbird. It applies to every key in the file.
keyImport.nothingToDo: Nothing in this source can be taken over that is not already here or unusable.
keyImport.failed: The keys could not be taken over
keyImport.wrongPassphrase: The passphrase does not match this key file.

note.sealedExternally: sealed by Thunderbird, take it over via the export instead
note.expired: expired, still useful for old messages
note.publicOnly: public half only, nothing can be decrypted with it
note.severalForOneAccount: several keys for this account, all are taken over and the newest becomes the active one

reason.unreadable: The key could not be read

keyImport.helpSummary: How do I get my own keys out of Thunderbird?
keyImport.helpStep1: In Thunderbird: Tools → OpenPGP Key Manager
keyImport.helpStep2: Select your own keys, then File → Backup Secret Keys To File
keyImport.helpStep3: Set a passphrase for the file, you will enter it here in a moment
keyImport.helpStep4: Click “From file …” here and pick the saved file

unlock.passwordWarning: With a password the entire database is encrypted: messages, contacts and credentials. Without it the app cannot connect to any server. There is no recovery: if the password is lost, the accounts have to be set up again.
unlock.confirmDelete: Delete profile "{{name}}" with all locally stored messages and credentials?

error.openFailed: This profile's database could not be opened.

profile.title: Profile
profile.name: Profile name
profile.encryptedHint: The database holding all messages, contacts and credentials is encrypted. Without the password the app cannot connect to any server.
profile.notEncryptedHint: Messages and credentials sit unencrypted on disk. A password is optional and can be removed again at any time.
profile.confirmRemovePassword: Turn off encryption? The database will be decrypted and left unencrypted on disk.
profile.autoLockHint: Locks the profile again when nothing happens for a while. The password is then required again.
profile.newHint: A separate profile with its own database and its own accounts, for a second person on the same machine, say. The open profile is left alone.
profile.newPasswordHint: With a password the new profile's database is encrypted. Without one it stays readable, and either way it can be changed later.
profile.nameTaken: That name is taken, in the chooser the two would be indistinguishable.
profile.newChooserHint: From the second profile onwards Peregrine asks which one to open at startup. That chooser is also where a profile can be deleted.

about.noUpdates: Peregrine does not check for updates on its own. A new version is installed by running the setup program again. Profiles are kept.

diagnostics.intro: Records what Peregrine sends to the servers and what comes back. Every line carries the gap to the previous line of the same connection. That is where the time goes.
diagnostics.ownClient: Use the built-in mail client for connections
diagnostics.ownClientHint: Experimental. Peregrine speaks IMAP itself instead of through the imapflow library. It applies the next time an account connects, for example after restarting Peregrine. If something misbehaves, switch it off again and report what happened.
diagnostics.recordHint: Off by default. Passwords are never recorded: for LOGIN and AUTHENTICATE the whole argument list is dropped, username included.
diagnostics.verboseHint: A sync produces thousands of them, pushing out the command flow you actually want to see.
diagnostics.empty: Nothing recorded. Switch recording on and trigger whatever you want to inspect.

savedSearch.queryHint: Same syntax as the search bar, e.g. from:anna has:attachment

pending.hint: Carried out without a connection. They will be sent on the next one, in the order they happened.
pending.failedHint: Tried several times without success. These changes happened here but not on the server. Click to discard them.
pending.scheduledHint: Waiting for the chosen moment, not for a connection. Click to call it back.
pending.cancelled: Called back, the message never left
pending.scheduledFailed: Could not read the scheduled messages
pending.waitingHint: Carried out without a connection and not yet at the server. Click to take individual ones back.
pending.waitingFailed: Could not read the waiting actions

snooze.localHint: Applies here only: on other devices the message stays in the inbox.

notifications.previewHint: Without the preview, a notification only says that something arrived, and for which account.
notifications.quietHint: Nothing appears during this window. Across midnight is allowed (22:00 to 07:00). Held-back notifications are not delivered later, mail from 3 a.m. is no longer new at 7.
notifications.perAccountHint: Unticked accounts stay silent. An account added later notifies again.

daily.title: Today
daily.empty: Nothing for today. Type an item here, or add a message from its context menu.
daily.fromMailHint: Messages carrying the configured tag. They leave this list when the tag goes, not by being ticked here.
daily.mailGone: The message this refers to can no longer be found

dailySettings.tagHint: Messages carrying this tag show up under "From the mailbox". They leave when the tag goes.
dailySettings.noTags: No tags yet, you can create them under Settings → Tags.
dailySettings.dayStartHint: Someone still working at one in the morning is having the evening before. Until this hour the previous day counts.
